content.comment_body: Hello, In my application, users set a weekly timer and I need to determine the total minutes in the selected interval. For instance, if the timer starts at 12:00 and ends at 13:01, that's 61 minutes. How can I obtain this value or is there an alternative method to process on/off timestamps? I need this calculation before the interval concludes, so I can't rely on standard timers or counters.
I've attached a possible solution for you.

Thank you very much, great job! I have 9 blocks of weekly timers, each with 2 cam inputs, totaling 18. That feels excessive. Is there a document showing which addresses to use? Is there a way to simplify, since I only use 6 blocks simultaneously?

The challenge stems from ON and OFF times being BCD-encoded, which is why so many blocks are required—four values fit in one word rather than four separate words. The VM addresses can be freely chosen; in a [product_name] diagram, you can use the range from VB0 to VB850. Edit: Times are transferred into the VM area using Parameter-VM-Mapping. The Parameter-VM-Mapping table allows up to 32 entries.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges calculating time intervals in minutes between weekly timer start and stop events within the [product_name] platform. The main issue is the BCD-encoding of time values, which complicates logic and increases the number of required blocks. There is a need for simpler documentation and easier address management for more efficient configurations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward method to compute minutes between two timer points, along with accessible guides and the ability to reduce the number of function blocks needed.
